evals.prompt: Grill me on this repo's answer to an incoming proposal from a sibling project. Repo pinned at <commit>. The proposal is at <path>. Use grill-with-counterpart with claude-delegate.
evals.expected_output: One grilling round presented by number: every delta with both answers verbatim under their own headings and surviving citations; every agreement labelled unverified, or unverifiable by agents where the question is owner, off-record or production; struck citations shown; the orchestrator's own answers written before dispatch; no file written by the counterpart.
expectations: The orchestrator's answers exist in .grill/round-1-orchestrator.md with a timestamp earlier than the dispatch
The brief sent to the counterpart contains the questions and no recommendation text
The brief names the pinned commit
Every delta shows the counterpart's recommendation verbatim under its own heading before the orchestrator's reading
Every agreement is labelled unverified; agreements on questions tagged owner, off-record or production are labelled unverifiable by agents
Every citation in both answer files carries a Direct, Inferred or struck tag
The counterpart's tree shows no changes (git status clean in its worktree)
A committed glossary entry that conflicts with the incoming proposal is presented as a delta or as the recorded answer, never silently replaced by the proposal's wording
A question the proposal answers but the owner decided differently on reaches the owner as a delta or an agreement, and is not settled by the agents
No question is closed on the ground that both agents agreed

evals.prompt: Same as eval 1, but the counterpart hits its quota and returns a failed result.json.
evals.expected_output: The round is presented to the owner from the orchestrator's answers alone, with the dropout stated; nothing waits on a re-dispatch.
expectations: The owner is told the counterpart dropped out, in the round's presentation
The round is presented with every question by number
At most one re-dispatch is attempted

ground_truth: An owner-approved spec in a private repo and the decision key extracted from it; kept off this repo. Run the eval against any settled decision of your own: pin the commit before the spec was written, give the counterpart the inputs the authors had, and score against what the owner actually decided.
